newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean stocks close at 1997 high of 738.12.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean stocks close at 1997 high of 738.12.

text.p: Hopes for an economic turnaround and sharply falling interest rates fuelled healthy buying interest in the Seoul stock market, sending share prices to a new 1997 high at the close.
The composite stock index gained 14.77 points, or 2.04 percent, to 738.12.
Brokers said the strengthening yen and a rise in export prices rekindled hopes of an economic turnaround.
The benchmark three-year corporate yields hit 11.98 percnet, the lowest level in three and a half months.
"The economic growth is now expected to be higher than the earlier forecast of five percent," said Kim Wan-hee of Dongsuh Securities.
He said an improvement in key export prices also helped to boost investor hopes.
Brokers said a sharp fall in interest rates sparked healthy buying interest of large-capitalised shares. The large-cap sub-index rose 3.32 percent, or 17.17 points, to 534.71.
"Investors expected a liquidity-driven market with sharply falling interest rates," said Casey Choe of Union Bank of Switzerland.
Choe said construction and financial companies with high financial costs would benefit from falling rates.
Kim of Dongsuh said some cheap large-cap manufacturing shares were in strong demand by foreign investors.
LG Electronics hit a 1997 high of 14,100, jumping to its daily higher-limit of 1,000 won. Electronic home appliance makers were seen a major beneficiary of an economic turnaround, brokers said.
Other blue chips also came into the spotlight. POSCO and KEPCO gained 1,400 won and 100 won to 58,600 and 26,100 respectively.
Semiconductor shares also gained momentum. Some brokers said an overnight rally in technology stocks on Wall Street was partially behind their strength in Seoul.
LG Semicon went limit up, gaining 2,600 won to 35,100, Hyundai Electronics rose 2,900 won to 42,900 and Samsung Electronics added 3,000 won to 64,500.
Merrill Lynch's influential analyst Tom Kurlak said he expected Micron Technology Inc to earn even more in 1997 and 1998 than he previously expected.
His comment spurred the demand for technology stocks, especially semiconductors, in New York markets.

"I cannot see any reason to revise our forecast upward for domestic semiconductor companies. It's too early to say the global memory chip industry has turned around," said Bahn Young-one of Ssangyong Securities.
Creditor banks on Wednesday agreed to extend a total of 15.9 billion won in emergency loans to Dainong Corp and Midopa Department Store 8000.KS, key units of the financially troubled Dainong Group.
Both Dainong Corp and Midopa Department Store went limit up, gaining 250 won and 660 won to 3,410 and 9,030 respectively.
